name: Procedural sound effects with ZzFX (horn, crash, siren, pickup, cash, mission, wasted, engine)
description: Synthesises a sound effect from the 21 ZzFX parameters exactly as ZzFX buildSamples does (with randomness off so the result is repeatable) and reports length, peak, RMS, sample checks and a ready zzfx(...) call. Includes eight game presets; no audio files are needed because the browser regenerates each sound from its parameters.
author: Skillpack contributors

provenance.license_check: GitHub API license field read and the license file itself read
provenance.primary_role: ZZFX.buildSamples synthesis (oscillator shapes, envelope, slide, pitch jump, repeat, noise, modulation, bit crush, delay, tremolo, biquad filter) and README example sounds
provenance.reference_values: Every case was generated by executing the pinned ZzFX.js buildSamples in Node.js with randomness 0 (reference/upstream_harness.mjs). Four cases are the upstream README examples; the int16 checksum of all samples matches exactly.

region.notes: Game rules are illustrative defaults, not real-world rules.

audit.principle: code decides, model explains, craftsman (usta) approves

usta_approval.what_to_check: that each event sound is recognisable, not too loud and not annoying when repeated (siren, engine).

external_audit.notes: Local tests only; no independent audit has been performed.

budget.enforcement: Raw CLI byte limit and POSIX alarm; strict schema, finite values and nesting checks; MCP subprocess killed/reaped after the timeout. One active calculation. Not a hostile-code sandbox.

dependencies.runtime: Python standard library plus jsonschema (schema check) only

data.logging: none; input contents are never logged or echoed in errors

mcp.instructions: One local deterministic tool. Explain its result and limits; the code decides, a human (usta) approves consequential use. No network access.

limitations: Randomness is forced to 0 for synthesis; the browser applies the stored randomness when playing, so live sounds vary slightly. Sounds are capped at 5 seconds. The browser plays ZzFXMicro, which multiplies by its master volume 0.3 and keeps samples in a plain array, so live samples differ from these Float32 values by tiny rounding in the delay path. Whether a sound is pleasant is a human judgement.
port_notes: Line-by-line port of ZZFX.buildSamples(v1.4.0) with JavaScript semantics reproduced: % as fmod, Math.round as floor(x+0.5), x|0 truncation, ++crush%0 being NaN (always recompute), the Float32Array buffer (Python array('f')) and the left-to-right biquad filter assignment order. Presets are original Skillpack choices except 'wasted', which is the upstream README 'Game Over' example.
flow_role: Step 8 (sesler): pick one sound per game event (horn, crash, siren, pickup, cash, mission_complete, wasted), check none clips (peak <= 1) and is longer than intended, then pass the parameter bank to G012. The HTML embeds ZzFXMicro (MIT) and plays zzfx(...params) on the event.
